subject: Total Quality Management-Department Elective IV
text: A company manufacturing chemical products has a well-established TQ program. SOL, Its most recent efforts involved preparing for ISO 9000 registration. This would help the company to gain competitive advantage. The firm hired additional staff to speed up the registration process. In the purchasing department, the additional work required to document the purchase of raw materials needed three additional employees, bringing the total number up to 10. All have been sincerely involved in the preparation for registration. Different types of raw materials are used, and ISO registration requires that each of their specifications be reviewed, updated and documented. One of the new employees focuses primarily on training the department’s employees in the new procedures. Purchasing agents see many potential benefits. Documentation of specifications will ensure more consistent purchases of materials. Training documentation allows the department to tell what training requirements will be needed by the new employees. In manufacturing, ISO appears to be just another quality program. In the past management would enthusiastically start the new program but after some time enthusiasm would die. Employees were never told that program had ended and never saw any benefits. Technicians saw no real incentives to participate and felt that management is simply forcing the program on the employees. They felt that employees on different shifts had their own way of performing their work, and that standard operating procedures would never be followed. The technicians compared the ISO efforts to a previous program on safety. With the safety program improvements were made at the insistence of the employees. The benefits that workers derived from safety program were quite evident but the benefits to be gained through ISO are not as clear.
